title: Financing Compute: The $1.8 Trillion Bet on AI Data Centers | BloombergNEF
gist: BNEF's survey of 2,000+ transactions finds data center developers raised at least $1.8 trillion since 2020 (nearly half in 3Q 2025-1H 2026), with private markets and complex credit-support structures (GPU-backed loans, residual-value guarantees, Nvidia's $198 billion-plus direct support) increasingly central, while at least $1 trillion of debt maturing within five years and an 18x jump in neocloud maturities from 2029 to 2030 create refinancing risk for smaller players like TeraWulf, Crusoe, Firmus and Nscale.

themes.theme: Scale and acceleration of capital raised

insights.claim: Data center developers raised at least $1.8 trillion across debt, equity and securitized instruments between 2020 and 1H 2026, with $794 billion, nearly half, raised between 3Q 2025 and 1H 2026.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Financing has sharply accelerated in the last year, raising the stakes of any credit market shift for AI capex.

insights.claim: Private markets supplied 56% of colocation financing in 1H 2026, and total financing for the large group of colocation providers exceeds that of the four hyperscalers.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Private credit is now the marginal funder of AI data centers; private credit vehicles carry concentrated exposure to colocation risk.

insights.claim: At least $1 trillion of data center debt matures within the next five years while markets price in higher credit risk, creating refinancing pressure.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: A refinancing wall into a higher-spread market is a key credit risk for the AI buildout over 2026-2031.

insights.claim: Rising interest rates, concerns about developers' debt levels and overreliance on financing support from hyperscalers and chipmakers are increasing refinancing pressure on data center firms.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Dependence on sponsor support is itself a risk factor; watch credit spreads on data center ABS and neocloud debt.

insights.claim: Neocloud maturing debt rises 18x year-over-year between 2029 and 2030, and colocation providers and neoclouds face steep increases in maturing debt volumes by 2030.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: A 2030 maturity cliff for neoclouds is a dated catalyst for credit stress if AI compute pricing softens.

insights.claim: Smaller developers such as TeraWulf and Crusoe face higher refinancing uncertainty because of large amounts of construction debt, and execution challenges have already affected Firmus and Nscale's high-valuation IPO plans.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Names to watch for credit stress or IPO repricing among smaller AI infrastructure developers.

insights.claim: Data center deal structures are becoming more complex, using credit support from investment-grade backers, including GPU-backed loans, direct guarantees, residual-value guarantees and prepayments, to let smaller developers raise capital at the size and tenor required.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Small developers' creditworthiness is borrowed; the true credit risk sits with the guarantor, so analyze backers rather than borrowers.

insights.claim: Nvidia has extended at least $198 billion in direct credit support to data center players, and has committed even more alongside large asset managers.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Nvidia is the single largest credit-support provider in AI data centers, making its balance-sheet policy systemic for the sector.

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley underwrote the most data center financing, driven partly by its close relationship with Meta, followed by Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Data center underwriting is a fee-revenue tailwind for these banks and concentrates their exposure to the AI capex cycle.

insights.claim: TD Bank and Scotiabank accelerated data center dealmaking the most in 2026, competing to fund established players.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Canadian banks are gaining share in AI infrastructure lending, a growing exposure to monitor.
